name: readability_first_unified_review_rubric

dimensions.rule: Retain the approved scope, order, and organizing classification.
Keep the opening, body sections, and synthesis focused on the review question.
Maintain a logical progression from scope and terminology through cases to synthesis and outlook.
Give every major section a stated role and a meaningful synthesis exit.
Avoid stitched extraction prose, repeated evidence-boundary boilerplate, and internal workflow language such as supplied evidence, evidence package, prompt, model, gate, or artifact labels.
Keep terminology, catalyst labels, and narrative voice consistent.
Retain valid figure provenance, placement, and identity boundaries.
State what each subsection contributes and what comparison it enables.
Cover the approved papers, section roles, scope axes, and evidence ceilings.
Distinguish anchor examples from extensions and explain their functions.
Use shared comparison axes and avoid unsupported rankings.
Keep case paragraphs within their assigned section and catalyst/mode boundary.
Close each substantive section with synthesis rather than a final isolated example.
Disclose missing metrics, untested classes, and evidence ceilings adjacent to interpretation.
Make each section's review function explicit rather than relying only on headings.
Use one principal example per case paragraph and meet the configured paragraph-length range.
Explain the paper's role in the review argument rather than listing extracted fields.
Build a continuous contribution-reaction-scope-limitation-significance progression.
Retain interpretation-changing conditions and evidence limits while compressing routine inventories.
Bound scope claims and do not relabel untested classes as failures.
Keep mechanism language at the evidence level supported by the source.
Tie practicality and comparison claims to shared reported axes.
Remove extraction scaffolds, label-style colons, fragments, duplicated sentences, and template transitions.
Map every case to stable paper IDs, local source paths, and citation records.
Preserve source-supported catalyst roles, primary assignment, and transformation identity.
Distinguish reported data, author inference, missing evidence, and review synthesis.
Do not fabricate metrics or silently change their denominator, basis, or stage.
Keep citations adjacent and aligned with the authoritative bibliography.
Separate untested, missing, inferred, and failed evidence states.
Respect the evidence boundary between primary sources, parsed records, and review synthesis.
Use detect-first independent review reports before synthesis or editing.
Do not invent data, methods, references, DOI values, mechanisms, structures, yields, selectivities, or interpretations.
Keep catalyst, ligand, reagent roles, and primary organizing assignment source-supported.
Preserve metric type, basis, and stage; do not interchange yield, conversion, recovery, selectivity, ee, er, dr, or de.
Do not silently reconcile catalyst loading, equivalents, concentration, temperature, time, atmosphere, pressure, or scale.
Protect stereochemical descriptors, formulas, chemical identifiers, and compound labels.
Keep observed results, explanations, proposed mechanisms, and review synthesis linguistically distinct; route wording-only calibration to final polish.
Base citation support on supplied/local records and mark unavailable support for verification.
Keep figure, caption, and nearby quantitative-claim identity linked to the source record.
Give every blocking finding a precise location, severity, confidence, and rewrite route.
Do not mechanically penalize passive methods-style prose; require meaning-preserving edits.
Report draft-quality and final-release state accurately without making the host's independent optional generation actions depend on this quality loop.

hard_regressions: missing linked source for a protected factual change
broken required figure path or unresolved figure identity
case paragraph outside the configured word range
label-style colon or extraction-field scaffold in generated case prose
